clue.text: Grannie, a nan possibly old inside?

definitions.text: Grannie, a nan possibly old inside?

indicators.note: inside asks for the single letter to be placed within the rearranged letters
possibly says these letters might be rearranged into some other form

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an elderly grandmother is very old at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the rearrangement and 'inside' the insertion. The whole clue also describes a grandmother in her nineties, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in their nineties is very old, and a grandmother is a typical example of such a person.

clue.text: Lost again, disorientated, provoking homesickness

indicators.note: disorientated means mixed up and confused, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: Getting lost yet again makes a traveller long for home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorientated' rearranges LOST AGAIN; 'provoking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful longing for home or the past is a synonym of homesickness.

clue.text: Part of gunpowder in gun, it recoils

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: Describing a gun kicking back when it is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'guN IT REcoils'; 'recoils' looks like a reversal signal but the run reads forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is an ingredient of traditional black powder.

clue.text: Devour pig's tail in blood

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: tail points to the final letter of the word pig

explanation.surface: Eating a pig's tail cooked in blood.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat greedily and in large amounts is a synonym of devour.

clue.text: They could be relatively helpful

parts.note: relatively is read as 'to relatives': people in power who give jobs to their family

explanation.definitionFit: People who favour their own relatives with jobs or advantages are guilty of favouritism toward kin.

clue.text: Mechanic concerned with pilot circling end of airstrip

indicators.note: circling says the first pieces go round the single letter

parts.note: re means concerning or about
an airman is one who flies aircraft

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word airstrip

explanation.surface: A mechanic worried about a pilot flying round over the runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' has both opening pieces go round the end letter of airstrip together, so it lands between them rather than inside the pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fixes machines is a mechanic in a general sense.

clue.text: Tart and redhead embraced by tart

indicators.note: embraced by says the letter is held inside the other piece

parts.note: acid means sour or tart
the head of the word red is R

explanation.surface: A tart and a redhead locked in an embrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Pungent and bitter in taste or smell, much like something tart.

clue.text: Criminal disturbance around street assembly

indicators.note: around says these pieces go on either side of the abbreviation

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a ruction is a noisy disturbance or row

explanation.surface: A criminal causing a commotion on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something together, or the thing built, is an assembly.

clue.text: 'Inception' filming location

definitions.meaning: a film is shot ..., read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A beginning or start of something is its inception; split, it is where filming happens.

clue.text: Put up again in bedroom, perhaps

definitions.text: Put up again in bedroom, perhaps

parts.words: Put up again in bedroom, perhaps
parts.note: put up suggests accommodating a guest again, but it means hanging wall coverings once more

explanation.definitionFit: Walls given a fresh covering of wallpaper have been decorated a second time.

clue.text: Discern corrupt indirect aims

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: Seeing through someone's crooked hidden motives.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell apart or perceive differences is to discern.

clue.text: Politicians dropping Socialist leader by Tory leader's account

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let fall out of that word

parts.note: statesmen are senior politicians

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the word Socialist
leader's points to the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: Politicians on the left losing their leader, as told by the Tory leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes one S out of STATESMEN to leave STATEMEN; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A written or spoken report of facts is an account.

clue.text: River trade missing Test

indicators.note: missing says part of that word is absent

parts.note: industry is trade or commerce
try means test or attempt

explanation.surface: Commerce on a river suffering without a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A major waterway of Pakistan, flowing from Tibet to the Arabian Sea.

clue.text: Rulers incorporating one metre units

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: regents rule in place of a monarch
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Measuring sticks that include a one-metre unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rulers' looks like measuring sticks beside 'metre'; it means governors.
explanation.definitionFit: Military units, such as army formations, are a kind of unit.

clue.text: 'Little Boy'? No, a smaller, older explosive device

definitions.text: 'Little Boy'? No, a smaller, older explosive device

parts.words: Little Boy'? No, a smaller, older explosive device
parts.note: Little Boy was the Hiroshima bomb; a very small person, a tiny man, is the name of an American missile

explanation.definitionFit: An American intercontinental ballistic missile is an explosive weapon, and the name splits as tiny plus adult male.

clue.text: Nabokov's first with the empty novel 'Lolita'

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the name Nabokov
novel means new, so the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Nabokov's first, empty novel, Lolita.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges THE EMPTY; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is the title character of Nabokov's novel, the archetypal sexually precocious young girl.

clue.text: He makes interest, saving endless readies initially

definitions.text: He makes interest, saving endless readies initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A man earning interest by saving cash without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'makes interest saving endless readies'; the whole clue paints the hoarder. Readies is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder who saves money endlessly to accumulate wealth is a skinflint.

clue.text: Secure rubbish in excess ends up here?

definitions.text: Secure rubbish in excess ends up here?

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole lot is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to moor is to make a boat secure

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
ends points to the first and last letters of the word excess

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Wondering where surplus junk gets stored away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes E and S from excess; 'in' puts ROT between them for EROTS; 'up' turns MOOREROTS to read backwards. The whole clue describes a place for excess junk.
explanation.definitionFit: A room for keeping surplus things safely is where junk and supplies are kept.

clue.text: 'Bond' feature with adult content

indicators.note: content means contents held inside, so the letter is inside the other word

parts.note: a chin is a facial feature
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A Bond film with adult content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007; it means a link or fetter. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Linked metal rings serve as a bond or fetter.

clue.text: Deceive girl, almost fashionable model

indicators.note: almost means not quite, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: miss is a young woman or girl
in means fashionable
a form is a model or pattern

explanation.surface: Misleading a girl who is nearly a trendy model.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone false information is to deceive or mislead them.

clue.text: At home, United in exercise process

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: PT is physical training, exercise
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Staying in for a home workout with the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Data entered into a computer is processed; to enter data is a computing process.

clue.text: Slug a mixture of drinks

definitions.meaning: slug means hit hard with the fist
a bowl of mixed fruit juice, spirits and spices served at parties

explanation.definitionFit: A hard blow with the fist, and also a party drink of mixed ingredients.

clue.text: Scot free, the man with bizarre character outside

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man

indicators.note: outside says that word goes round the other

parts.note: Mr Bean is a bizarre comic character from British television
rid means free, as in rid of

explanation.surface: A Scotsman got off scot-free with an odd fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bean is a British TV comedy character played by Rowan Atkinson. 'Scot free' looks like the phrase scot-free; Scot is the definition. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Western Isles off Scotland's coast is a kind of Scot.

clue.text: Thank Queen covering live opening…

indicators.note: covering says the name goes over and around the letter

parts.note: Good Queen Bess is Elizabeth I

indicators.note: opening points to the first letter of the word live

explanation.surface: Thanking the Queen for opening a live broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: To give thanks or praise, especially to God, is an older sense of thank.

clue.text: …keen on catching Queen opening

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: into means keen on, as in being into music
R is the abbreviation for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: A fan keen on a Queen song's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots link this to the previous clue's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief introductory section is an opening.

clue.text: Grandma's remote, sadly getting very short measure

parts.note: nan is a grandmother

indicators.note: sadly means badly or in a sorry state, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grandma's TV remote has gone, sadly losing its measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges REMOTE to OMETRE; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a metre is a very short unit of length.

clue.text: Hawk catching river fish

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: to hawk is to tout or sell

explanation.surface: A hawk swooping to catch a river fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' looks like the bird; it means sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Herds turn to stampeding mass in bad weather

indicators.note: stampeding animals rush wildly, so these letters scatter

explanation.surface: Herds of cattle panic and stampede in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stampeding' rearranges HERDS TURN TO; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm with lightning and thunder is a spell of bad weather.
